out‐wintering of in‐calf heifers on fodderbeet and perennial ryegrass was not detrimental to the peripartum performance of the heifer and the subsequent milk yield of the first‐lactation cow.

winter feeding of dairy heifers on perennial ryegrasses or fodder beet is a feasible alternative to housing, with no detrimental effects on periparturition performance or milk production and metabolism.

the peripartum performance and metabolism of dairy heifers out‐winted on fodder beet, perennial ryegrass, or housed and fed a concentrate and grass silage diet.
the effect of different wintering systems on the performance and metabolism of dairy cows during late pregnancy, parturition and early lactation.

out‐wintered heifers had similar periparturition performance and early lactation milk yield compared with housed heifers.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the out‐wintering of pregnant Holstein-Friesian heifers on perennial ryegrasses or fodder beet and grass forage is a viable alternative for wintering heifers in a high output TMR-based system in the UK, and can be used to reduce costs of winter feeding.
out‐wintered heifers had similar performance to housed heifers and were not disadvantaged in terms of body condition score, milk yield or composition.
out‐wintered heifers can perform well in a high‐output T MR‐based system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
out‐wintered heifers can perform as well as those housed and fed a concentrate‐based diet.
out‐wintered heifers can achieve similar performance to housed heifers, with a potential to reduce costs and improve animal welfare.

the use of fodder beet in winter grazing systems can support the performance of dairy heifers in the peripartum period, but this needs to be balanced against the potential negative impact of lower milk fat content in the early lactation period.
